title: [CQ-R10a] Signal-safe guest job teardown
definitionOfDone: During relay(), SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT sent to the supervisor each SIGKILL and reap the job's whole session group (including a grandchild that ignores SIGTERM), leave no agent socket or connection behind, write no observation frame, and exit with one new documented code; one real-process test per signal proves it.

A SIGKILL of the supervisor leaves no process of the job's session alive within 5 seconds, proven by a Linux real-process test whose job has a grandchild (the row skips off Linux with a reason); a normal relay completion never triggers that kill path.

Signal dispositions are restored on every relay() exit path, SIGCHLD stays SIG_DFL, the file stays stdlib-only, main() still returns 78, and every existing test in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs passes unchanged.
A fresh `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

Test changes (scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs):
- S12 extended. Before the calls, the harness sets its own non-blocking wakeup fd. Each of the 6 exit paths (0/71/74/74/76/75) now also asserts:

- New S15, deterministic RED for QA's race, no gdb needed. A helper thread `signal.pthread_kill`s itself with SIGTERM 0.5 s after the job's output frame. CPython runs the C handler on that thread, so the main thread's blocked syscall sees no EINTR. That is the same state as QA's gdb repro, a signal landing after the last Python check but before the syscall blocks.
  - Two rows: a quiet job blocks the wait in pump's select; a job that dup2s /dev/null over fds 1-2 blocks it in the last start-pipe read.

  - spawnSync uses killSignal SIGKILL, because a timeout's SIGTERM would itself wake the hung wait.
- New S16. A signal relay() does not handle (a caller SIGUSR1 handler, sent by the job) still reaches the caller, relay returns 0, and its CPU time stays under 0.5 s. This guards the drain: an undrained wakeup byte would spin the select for the job's whole second.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN in scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py. The architect validated this exact design on a scratch copy: 41/41 tests green, runtime diff +102/-9. In that run, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT emptied the session in 0.04 s, so did a SIGKILL of the supervisor, and a normal completion left a lingering grandchild alive.

MECHANISM
- The supervisor no longer execs the job directly. It starts GUARD, an inline stdlib Python program, as the job's session leader, with start_new_session and pass_fds (two pipes).
- GUARD runs the job as its child in the same process group, so S4, S5 and S6 keep their meaning.
- GUARD exits with the job's status: a code passes through, and a terminating signal is re-raised with core files disabled. The observation is therefore unchanged.
- If GUARD's life pipe reaches EOF while it lives (the supervisor died before reaping it), GUARD SIGKILLs its own group. Its own live membership pins that group id, so no reused pgid can be hit. This is the uncatchable-SIGKILL defence. It needs no root, ctypes or cgroups, and it is portable to macOS.
- A stand-down byte, written after the output pipes close, lets GUARD exit once the job has exited, so a normal completion never kills.
- The start pipe carries '+' once the job is running, and EOF once GUARD has exited.
- For catchable signals, Termination raises Terminated ONLY inside wait(). Only pump's select() and the two start-pipe reads are wrapped in it. A signal therefore can never cut a finally short, and a second signal during teardown is only recorded.
- relay() becomes a wrapper that installs the three handlers and restores them on every path.

EDITS
(1) Header exit-code list: replace the 74/76 part with: '74 I/O failure or host EOF (child group killed); 75 SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGINT (child group killed, no\n# observation); 76 host protocol violation (child group killed); 77 not root; 78 root bridge with no job.'
(2) Directly after CODE = re.compile(...):
# CQ-R10a: these end relay() through its teardown; SIGKILL of the supervisor is left to GUARD.
TERMINATION_SIGNALS = (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIGINT)
EX_TERMINATED = os.EX_TEMPFAIL
# The job's session leader. It runs the job in its own group and exits with the job's status. On EOF of the life pipe
# (the supervisor died before reaping it) it SIGKILLs that group, whose id this live member pins. A stand-down byte,
# sent after the output pipes close, lets it exit once the job has; the start pipe gets '+' once the job runs, and
# EOF once this process is gone.
GUARD = '''import os, resource, signal, subprocess, sys, threading
life, start = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
for fd in (life, start):
    os.set_inheritable(fd, False)
for number in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIGINT):
    signal.signal(number, lambda *_: None)  # group-wide signals are for the job; a caught signal resets at its exec
released = threading.Event()
def watch():
    while True:
        if not os.read(life, 1):
            os.killpg(0, signal.SIGKILL)  # the supervisor died; this live leader pins the group id
        released.set()
threading.Thread(target=watch, daemon=True).start()
try:
    job = subprocess.Popen(sys.argv[3:])
except Exception:
    os._exit(1)  # no '+': the supervisor reports EX_OSERR
try:
    os.write(start, b'+')
    null = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_RDWR)
    os.dup2(null, 1)
    os.dup2(null, 2)  # only the job and its descendants hold the output pipes
    status = os.waitpid(job.pid, 0)[1]
    released.wait()
except BaseException:
    os.killpg(0, signal.SIGKILL)  # never orphan a started job
code = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
if code >= 0:
    os._exit(code)
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))  # die by the job's signal without writing a core file
if -code not in (signal.SIGKILL, signal.SIGSTOP):
    signal.signal(-code, signal.SIG_DFL)
os.kill(os.getpid(), -code)
os._exit(128 - code)
'''
(3) After class ProtocolViolation:
class Terminated(Exception):
    """A termination signal reached relay(); the bridge ends with EX_TERMINATED."""


class Termination:
    """Raises Terminated only inside wait(), so a signal can never cut teardown short."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.caught = self.armed = False

    def handle(self, number, frame):
        self.caught = True
        if self.armed:
            self.armed = False
            raise Terminated

    def wait(self, call, *args):
        self.armed = True
        try:
            if self.caught:
                raise Terminated
            return call(*args)
        finally:
            self.armed = False
(4) pump:
- signature: def pump(child, out_fd, bridge, wait=lambda call: call()):
- loop line: for key, mask in wait(selector.select):
(5) Keep relay()'s preceding comment and its SIGCHLD reset line. Then:
    termination = Termination()
    saved = [(number, signal.signal(number, termination.handle)) for number in TERMINATION_SIGNALS]
    try:
        return run_bridge(argv, out_fd, in_fd, agent_socket, agent_uid, peer_uid, termination)
    except Terminated:
        return EX_TERMINATED  # run_bridge's finally has killed and reaped the group and closed the bridge
    finally:
        for number, handler in saved:
            signal.signal(number, signal.SIG_DFL if handler is None else handler)


def run_bridge(argv, out_fd, in_fd, agent_socket, agent_uid, peer_uid, termination):
The rest of the old relay body moves here with exactly these changes:
- after `bridge = Bridge(out_fd, peer_uid)`:
    life, life_end = os.pipe()  # the guard reads life; this process holds life_end until the guard is reaped
    start_end, start = os.pipe()  # the guard writes '+' once the job runs; EOF means the guard has exited
- Popen becomes:
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', '-c', GUARD, str(life), str(start), *argv], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True, pass_fds=(life, start))
- its except also closes life_end and start_end before `return os.EX_OSERR`;
- add `finally: os.close(life); os.close(start)` to that same try;
- the main try starts:
    if termination.wait(os.read, start_end, 1) != b'+':
        return os.EX_OSERR  # the guard could not start the job
    pump(child, out_fd, bridge, termination.wait)
    os.write(life_end, b'0')  # stand down: a normal completion never kills the group
    termination.wait(os.read, start_end, 1)  # EOF: the guard has exited with the job's status
    # Both pipes are at EOF and the guard has exited; waitpid is the only source of the exit frame.
  then the existing reap, observation and return 0;
- the teardown comment becomes: Kill the whole session group while the unreaped guard (its leader) still pins its id, then reap it.
- the finally also closes life_end and start_end, before bridge.close().

ERROR HANDLING
Every existing path keeps its code:
- Popen or bridge.open failure: 71.
- The guard sends no '+': 71, after the finally kills and reaps the guard.
- Host EOF or stdout failure: 74.
- Protocol violation: 76.
- Terminated: 75, from the wrapper, after run_bridge's finally has killed and reaped the group and closed the bridge.

Unchanged: bridgeArgv, the frames, Bridge, main() (still 78), the shebang and the stdlib-only rule.

Re-run the new tests, then the whole file: all green.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN, QA fix: no wait in relay() can lose a termination signal any more. This follows the stdlib route QA suggested, signal.set_wakeup_fd on a self-pipe. Changes to scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py:

- Termination.__init__ creates wake_r/wake_w with os.pipe(), which is non-inheritable by PEP 446, and makes both non-blocking. set_wakeup_fd requires that of wake_w, and drain() must never block on wake_r.
- New Termination.drain(*_) reads up to 4096 bytes from wake_r and tolerates BlockingIOError. The bytes only wake a wait; handle() still records the signal.
- New Termination.read(fd) replaces both `termination.wait(os.read, start_end, 1)` calls:
  - It opens a `with selectors.DefaultSelector()` on fd plus wake_r.
  - It loops over `self.wait(selector.select)`, draining until fd is reported, then reads one byte with os.read(fd, 1).
  - A signal therefore either raises inside the armed select, through EINTR or the wakeup byte, or sets `caught`, and the next wait() raises.
- run_bridge registers wake_r in bridge.selector with data=termination.drain, inside the try that maps OSError to 71. pump's existing `key.data(key, mask)` dispatch drains it, so pump itself is unchanged.
- relay():
  - `wakeup = signal.set_wakeup_fd(termination.wake_w, warn_on_full_buffer=False)` runs before the handlers are installed;
  - the finally restores the handlers (LIFO), then `signal.set_wakeup_fd(wakeup)`, then closes both ends. Closing comes last, so no signal byte can reach a reused fd number.
- QA's taste notes, also applied:
  - pump's unused `wait=lambda call: call()` default is gone;
  - GUARD's redundant `os.set_inheritable(life/start, False)` loop is gone. GUARD's Popen keeps close_fds=True, and S4 proves the job holds no fd beyond 0-2.
- Unchanged: the frames, bridgeArgv, codes 0/64/71/74/76/77/78, the main()=78 path, GUARD's mechanism and the SIGCHLD reset. The file stays stdlib-only.

Adversarial review of round 2 (wakeup fd), plus QA evidence (a)-(d). The review found two things and changed bytes, so the gate was re-run fresh.

1) New defect: S9 also flaked with ECONNRESET. No hang was involved, and the cause predates this round. 30 S9-only runs each, same load (~15): round-1 supervisor 32da7f7 failed 7/30, pre-fix HEAD failed 8/30, every failure `read ECONNRESET` on the agent socket.
- Cause: S9 signals as soon as Node reports 'connect'. On AF_UNIX that fires once the connection is queued, before accept. If Terminated wins, bridge.close() closes the listener and Linux resets the queued connection.
- Probe: a queued connection whose listener closes gets ConnectionResetError 104; one accepted and then closed reads b''.

- S9 is untouched. guarded() gained an optional job parameter (default GROUP_JOB), so S9 and S10 run with identical inputs.
- New S17 (deterministic): the job closes its output, so pump stops polling the listener; an agent connects 0.5 s later and stays queued; SIGTERM. It expects 75 and a clean close. HEAD supervisor: 3/3 ECONNRESET (RED). Fix: 3/3 pass.

reopenReason:
DoD1 and DoD4 fail on a reproducible lost-wakeup race in Termination.wait(); the step-4 note calls it a "residual".

My fresh run of the DoD gate exited 1: S9 SIGHUP timed out after 30 s, and of 43 tests, 42 passed and 1 was cancelled. Five more fresh runs passed, so the gate is intermittent, not green.

Root cause: wait() checks `caught`, then enters a blocking syscall (epoll_wait, or read(2) on start_end). A TERM/HUP/INT delivered between the two only trips CPython's C-level flag, and no fd wakes the syscall. So the supervisor stays blocked until an unrelated fd event, which never comes for a quiet job. Meanwhile the job group keeps running, the bridge stays open and there is no exit 75.

I reproduced this deterministically with gdb (comment-63cccd6c on this task). SIGHUP delivered at pump's idle epoll_wait entry left the supervisor in do_epoll_wait with no signal pending, and the job and grandchild alive. One extra fd event then gave exit 75. The control, a SIGHUP while the supervisor was already blocked, exited 75 promptly. Neither the DoD nor the plan's residual list accepts this, and the objective says relay() must never leave its job running when the supervisor is terminated.

Verified OK, keep as is:
- The completion commit 32da7f7 on moe/work-2026-10-24: runtime +108/-9 and tests +141/-2, existing tests unchanged.
- DoD2: S10 and S11.
- DoD3: S12, S7 and main()=78.
- S13 and S14.
- Four scratch mutants were each killed by their target test.
- Windows Node 24.16: 19 pass, 24 skip, 0 fail.
- No __pycache__.

Non-blocking taste notes, not grounds: pump's unused `wait` default, and GUARD's redundant set_inheritable.

comments.content:
QA evidence for the rejection: the lost wakeup in Termination.wait() (qa-6fa5d758, 2026-10-27).

1) Gate. A fresh run of env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs exited 1. Setup: node v24.21.0, Python 3.12.3, WSL2, load about 14 on 16 cores, 15:27:42Z.
- 43 tests: 42 pass, 0 fail, 1 cancelled.
- "S9 SIGHUP during relay() ..." timed out after 30000ms.
- Five more full runs each passed 43/43.

2) Mechanism. In guest-supervisor.py, Termination.wait() (L102-109) sets armed, checks `caught`, then calls the blocking syscall: pump's selector.select (L301) or os.read(start_end) (L358/L365).
- A signal delivered after CPython's last eval-breaker check (in EpollSelector.select, after max()) but before epoll_wait/read(2) starts runs only the C handler. It trips a flag, and no wakeup fd is set.
- CPython runs the Python handler only when the syscall returns. For S9's quiet job and idle agent, that never happens.
- The final start_end read after stand-down has the same window. It waits as long as a job that closed fds 1-2 keeps running.

3) Deterministic gdb repro (gdb as the harness's parent, so it works with ptrace_scope=1). The files are in /tmp/claude-1000/qa-r10a/gdb-c28u: harness.py, common.gdb, inject.gdb, control.gdb, driver.py.
- Run: python3 -I -B driver.py <repo>/scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py inject /tmp/claude-1000/qa-r10a/gdb-c28u (then the same with `control`).
- harness.py runs m.relay(['python3','-I','-c',GROUP_JOB], out_fd=<file>, in_fd=r, agent_socket=<path>, agent_uid=os.getuid()).
- common.gdb: set startup-with-shell off; handle SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGCHLD/SIGPIPE nostop noprint pass.
- inject.gdb: tbreak epoll_wait; ignore $bpnum 1; commands: signal SIGHUP. This delivers SIGHUP at the entry of pump's idle select, once the output frame is out.

RESULT (inject):
- 3 s after the SIGHUP, the supervisor is alive.
- wchan=do_epoll_wait, syscall 232, SigPnd=ShdPnd=0 (the signal was consumed), SigCgt=0x4003.
- The job and grandchild are ALIVE, and there are 0 observation frames.
- One agent connect (a single fd event) then gives exit 75 (gdb: "exited with code 0113"), and the job and grandchild are gone.

RESULT (control): a SIGHUP sent while the supervisor is already blocked gives a prompt 75 with the group gone.

4) Verified fine, keep as is:
- The diff: runtime +108/-9 and tests +141/-2, existing tests untouched.
- S10-S14.
- Four scratch mutants each killed by their target: watch never kills (S10), no handlers (S9), kill instead of killpg (S9), and close instead of stand-down (S11).
- Windows Node 24.16: 19 pass, 24 skip, 0 fail.
- No __pycache__.

Fix direction: any TERM/HUP/INT inside relay() must end it promptly with 75, without waiting for another fd event. The stdlib way is signal.set_wakeup_fd() on a non-blocking, non-inheritable pipe:
- register its read end in bridge.selector (drained);
- make both start_end waits also watch it;
- on every relay() exit path, restore the previous wakeup fd and close the pipe.
Or bound each wait with a short timeout that re-checks `caught`. Re-run the gdb recipe after the fix: inject must exit 75 with no extra fd event.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected alternatives:
(1) prctl PR_SET_PDEATHSIG via ctypes. It only reaches the direct child (it is not inherited by grandchildren), it is Linux-only, and it needs a getppid race check.
(2) A per-job cgroup v2 with cgroup.kill. It needs root or delegation, so it cannot be proven by unprivileged tests, and something must still write cgroup.kill once the supervisor is gone.
(3) A sibling guard. It sits outside the job's session, so once init reaps the leader it could signal a reused pgid.
(4) A watcher forked in preexec_fn. It becomes an unexpected child of the job, and must dodge subprocess's errpipe.
(5) An always-raising handler. A signal at the first bytecode of a finally would skip the teardown. Arming only inside wait() closes that hole.
(6) A 'guard' CLI mode of the supervisor file. The decision memory forbids extra CLI modes, so GUARD is an inline -c program whose imports S12 checks.

Exit code: 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL), because the host session (guest-session.mjs) treats every non-zero provider exit as SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED, so no code collides.
planningNotes.risks:
- Signal-safety: never raise from the handler outside Termination.wait().
- Pid reuse: kill a group only while a live or unreaped member pins it.
- Orphans: a failing or mutated run can leave sleepers, so kill only your own after each run (gotcha).
- Never let __pycache__ land in scripts/local-runner (-B).
- The guard changes the job's parent (the guard, not the supervisor) and adds a python3 start per relay.
- R10 final will add the privilege drop in the guard's Popen.
- dependsOn CQ-R08 (task-7a77465, REVIEW, landed b0e5982) must be DONE before a worker claims this task.

completionSummary:
CQ-R10a rework 2, after QA reject 1. No wait in relay() can lose a termination signal, and the job never outlives a terminated supervisor.
guest-supervisor.py (vs 32da7f7~1: +136/-9):
- QA fix: set_wakeup_fd on Termination's non-blocking pipe. wake_r is in bridge.selector, drained; both start-pipe reads use Termination.read() (fd plus wake_r). relay() restores the caller's wakeup fd and closes the pipe on every path. Terminated still raises only inside wait().
- New: Bridge.close() accepts at most 2*MAX_CONNECTIONS queued connections before closing, so peers read EOF. This fixes a pre-existing S9 flake: 7/30 S9-only runs on 32da7f7 hit ECONNRESET, because AF_UNIX 'connect' fires once a connection is queued and closing the listener resets it.
- QA's taste notes applied.
Tests (+219/-2; the 35 pre-existing tests are byte-identical; S9 not edited):
- S12 also checks the wakeup fd is restored and no fd leaks on all 6 paths.
- S15: pthread_kill lost-wakeup emulation (pump, last read); RED on old code.
- S16: a caller SIGUSR1 causes no spin (pump, last read).
- S17: a queued connection reads EOF; RED 3/3 pre-fix.
- guarded() takes an optional job.
QA evidence:
- (b) gdb, QA's driver: before, a hang in do_epoll_wait with SigPnd=0 until an extra fd event; after, exit 75 before the first 50 ms poll, job and grandchild gone (ignore 2, since read('+') now polls).
- (c) 30x '^S9 ': 30/30, 0 ECONNRESET, 0 timeouts.
- (d) Fresh gate exit 0, 46/46; 5 repeat gates 46/46 each.
Mutation: 17/17 scratch mutants killed by their target tests. Windows Node 24.16: 19 pass, 27 skip, 0 fail.
Residuals:
- relay() owns the process-wide wakeup fd while it runs; main() sets none.
- A TERM after GUARD's exit is absorbed: exit 0 with the observation.
- Connections queued past 2*MAX_CONNECTIONS at close are still reset.
- Round 1's residuals stand.

issues.description: QA fresh DoD4 gate (env -i Node v24.21.0 PATH, Python 3.12.3, WSL2, 2026-10-27T15:27:42Z) exited 1: 43 tests, 42 pass, 1 cancelled. 'S9 SIGHUP during relay() ... exits 75 with no observation' timed out after 30000ms. Five more fresh runs passed 43/43, so the gate is intermittent, not green. S9 is a correct spec, and the supervisor is at fault (next issue). Do not edit or weaken S9 or any existing test.

Lost wakeup: Termination.wait() (L102-109; pump select L301, start_end reads L358/L365) checks `caught`, then blocks. A TERM/HUP/INT landing after CPython's last eval-breaker check but before epoll_wait or read(2) starts only trips the C-level flag, and no fd wakes the syscall. The supervisor then blocks until an unrelated fd event, which never comes for a quiet job: the group lives on and there is no exit 75. gdb repro and results are in my task comment. This is a DoD1 defect, not a residual.

Fix: any TERM/HUP/INT inside relay() must end it promptly with 75, never waiting for an unrelated fd event. Stdlib way: a non-blocking, non-inheritable self-pipe set via signal.set_wakeup_fd() in relay(), its read end in bridge.selector (drained), and both start_end waits also watching it; restore the previous wakeup fd and close the pipe on every exit path. Alternative: bound each blocking wait with a short timeout that re-checks `caught`. Codes, frames and GUARD are unchanged.

Evidence: (a) If set_wakeup_fd is used, extend S12 to assert the caller's wakeup fd is restored on all 6 exit paths (sentinel fd set before each call, compared via the set_wakeup_fd return after it). (b) Record the gdb recipe before/after the fix in a step note: before, a hang until an extra fd event; after, a prompt 75 with the job and grandchild gone. (c) Run `--test-name-pattern='^S9 '` 30 times with no timeout. (d) Run a fresh full gate, exit 0, and pass it to complete_task.

rejectionHistory.reason:
DoD1 and DoD4 fail on a reproducible lost-wakeup race in Termination.wait(); the step-4 note calls it a "residual".

My fresh run of the DoD gate exited 1: S9 SIGHUP timed out after 30 s, and of 43 tests, 42 passed and 1 was cancelled. Five more fresh runs passed, so the gate is intermittent, not green.

Root cause: wait() checks `caught`, then enters a blocking syscall (epoll_wait, or read(2) on start_end). A TERM/HUP/INT delivered between the two only trips CPython's C-level flag, and no fd wakes the syscall. So the supervisor stays blocked until an unrelated fd event, which never comes for a quiet job. Meanwhile the job group keeps running, the bridge stays open and there is no exit 75.

I reproduced this deterministically with gdb (comment-63cccd6c on this task). SIGHUP delivered at pump's idle epoll_wait entry left the supervisor in do_epoll_wait with no signal pending, and the job and grandchild alive. One extra fd event then gave exit 75. The control, a SIGHUP while the supervisor was already blocked, exited 75 promptly. Neither the DoD nor the plan's residual list accepts this, and the objective says relay() must never leave its job running when the supervisor is terminated.

Verified OK, keep as is:
- The completion commit 32da7f7 on moe/work-2026-10-24: runtime +108/-9 and tests +141/-2, existing tests unchanged.
- DoD2: S10 and S11.
- DoD3: S12, S7 and main()=78.
- S13 and S14.
- Four scratch mutants were each killed by their target test.
- Windows Node 24.16: 19 pass, 24 skip, 0 fail.
- No __pycache__.

Non-blocking taste notes, not grounds: pump's unused `wait` default, and GUARD's redundant set_inheritable.
